# Further Reading {#sec-fr11}

Curious whether random forest is *really* your best option in
[Workshop 8](workshop_8.qmd#sec-w8-part2)?

There are *so many* machine learning methods and *even more*
possible R packages ("engines") that are supported in the 
`parnsip` R package. For more information on these
possibilities, see the 
[model types, engines and arguments guide](https://www.tidymodels.org/find/parsnip/). 

The tidymodels
[tuning and comparing models tutorial](https://workflowsets.tidymodels.org/articles/tuning-and-comparing-models.html)
shows how to compare it against several other classification
algorithms.

If you'd like to explore these ideas further, see the tidymodels
tutorials on
[feature engineering](https://www.tidymodels.org/books/fes/),
[cross-validation](https://www.tidymodels.org/start/resampling/),
[hyperparameter tuning](https://www.tidymodels.org/start/tuning/),
and
[multi-model comparison](https://workflowsets.tidymodels.org/articles/tuning-and-comparing-models.html).

The tidyclust package provides functions for k-means and hierarchical
clustering methods, among more, as well as how to tune these cluster
models. For more information, see the
[tidyclust documentation](https://tidyclust.tidymodels.org).

## Glossary {#sec-glossary}

::: {#artificial-intelligence}
**Artificial Intelligence.** The broad field of computer science
focused on building systems that simulate human-like reasoning,
learning, and decision-making.
:::

::: {#machine-learning}
**Machine Learning.** A subset of AI where systems learn patterns
from data to make decisions or predictions without being explicitly
programmed.
:::

::: {#unsupervised-ml}
**Unsupervised ML.** A type of ML where a model finds hidden patterns
or groupings in unlabelled data (e.g. clustering, dimensionality
reduction).
:::

::: {#supervised-ml}
**Supervised ML.** A type of ML where a model is trained on labelled
data, learning to map inputs to known outputs.
:::

::: {#engines}
**Engines.** A computational system or framework that executes a
model or algorithm to process data and produce outputs.
:::

::: {#model}
**Model.** A mathematical representation learned from data that
captures patterns and can be used to make predictions or decisions on
new inputs.
:::

::: {#learning}
**Learning.** The process by which an algorithm iteratively adjusts
its internal parameters based on data to improve its performance on a
task.
:::

::: {#predicting}
**Predicting.** The application of a trained model to new, unseen
data to produce an estimated output.
:::

::: {#pca}
**Principal Components Analysis.** A dimensionality reduction
technique that transforms data into a smaller set of uncorrelated
variables that capture the most variance.
:::

::: {#mds}
**Multidimensional Scaling.** A technique that visualises the
similarity or dissimilarity between data points by mapping them into
a lower-dimensional space.
:::

::: {#tree-clustering}
**Tree-based Clustering.** A hierarchical clustering approach that
organises data into a tree structure, grouping similar observations
at successive levels of granularity.
:::

::: {#k-means}
**K-means Clustering.** An unsupervised clustering algorithm that
partitions observations into *k* groups by iteratively assigning each
point to its nearest centroid and updating centroids until they
stabilise.
:::

::: {#hierarchical-clustering}
**Hierarchical Clustering.** An unsupervised clustering approach that
builds a dendrogram by repeatedly merging the two closest samples or
clusters, without requiring the number of clusters to be fixed in
advance.
:::

::: {#train-test-split}
**Train/Test Split.** Dividing a dataset into a training set (used to
fit a model) and a held-out test set (used to evaluate performance on
unseen data).
:::

::: {#confusion-matrix}
**Confusion Matrix.** A table comparing predicted class labels
against true labels, with diagonal cells showing correct predictions
and off-diagonal cells showing misclassifications.
:::

::: {#auroc-auprc}
**AUROC / AUPRC.** Area Under the ROC Curve / Area Under the
Precision-Recall Curve — summary metrics of classification
performance across all thresholds; AUPRC is more sensitive to class
imbalance than AUROC.
:::

::: {#recipe}
**Recipe (tidymodels).** A tidymodels object that specifies the
preprocessing steps (e.g. normalisation, dummy encoding) applied to
data before a model is fit.
:::

::: {#workflow}
**Workflow (tidymodels).** A tidymodels object that bundles a
preprocessing recipe and a model specification together so they are
applied consistently during fitting and prediction.
:::

::: {#silhouette-score}
**Silhouette Score.** A per-observation metric ranging from -1 to +1
that measures how similar an observation is to its own cluster
compared to the nearest neighbouring cluster; higher values indicate
better-separated clusters.
:::

::: {#dendrogram}
**Dendrogram.** A tree diagram produced by hierarchical clustering
that records the order in which samples or clusters are merged,
allowing the number of clusters to be chosen by cutting the tree at a
given height.
:::

::: {#hyperparameter}
**Hyperparameter.** A model setting (e.g. `mtry`, `k`) chosen before
training that controls how a model learns, as distinct from
parameters estimated from the data itself.
:::

::: {#cross-validation}
**Cross-validation.** A resampling technique that repeatedly splits
data into folds, training on some and evaluating on the rest, to
obtain a more robust estimate of model performance than a single
split.
:::

::: {#random-forest}
**Random Forest.** An ensemble of many decision trees, each trained
on a random bootstrap sample of the data and a random subset of
predictors at each split; averaging their predictions reduces
overfitting relative to a single tree.
:::

## Tidymodels {#tidy-table-steps}

package | step | functions | 
--------|--------|--------|
rsample | 1. split into test and train sets | `initial_split()`, `training()`, `testing()` | 
recipes | 2. create recipe and assign variable rols | `recipe()`, `update_role()`| 
parsnip | 3. specify model, engine and mode | e.g., `set_engine()`, `set_mode()`, `rand_forest()` | 
workflows | 4. create workflow, add recipe, add model | `workflow()`, `add_recipe()`, `add_model()` |
parsnip | 5. fit workflow | `fit()` | 
parsnip | 6. get predictions | `predict()` |
yardstick | 7. use predictions to get performance metrics | `rmse()`, `accuracy()`, `metrics()` | 

Another tutorial that summarises these aspects can be found
[here](https://chenxing.space/blog/tidymodels-ecosystem-tutorial/).

## Tidymodels vs. Tidyclust {#tidymodelclust}

Several tidymodels functions have tidyclust equivalents that are
written differently; these should be used when working with
clustering workflows:

| `tidymodels` Function   | `tidyclust` Equivalent          | Same |
|-------------------------|---------------------------------|------|
| `collect_metrics()`	    | `collect_metrics()`             | ✅   |
| `select_best()`	        | `select_best()`                 | ✅   |
| `fit()`	                | `fit()`                         | ✅   |
| `predict()`	            | `predict()`                     | ✅   |
| `tune_grid()`	          | `tune_cluster()`                | ❌   |   
| `finalise_workflow()`	  | `finalise_workflow_tidyclust()` | ❌   |   
| `metric_set()`	        | `cluster_metric_set()`          | ❌   |
